build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player character moves freely in a bounded arena with 360-degree aiming and firing toward the mouse cursor. Score 0 if there is no movement or aiming.
Enemies spawn in organized waves with clear wave-start announcements, escalating in count and variety with each wave. Score 0 if enemies spawn randomly with no wave structure.
Between waves a shop or upgrade prompt offers weapon and defense upgrades purchased with earned currency, visibly changing subsequent combat. Score 0 if no between-wave upgrades exist.
A screen-clearing airstrike or special ability can be triggered with limited charges, destroying all on-screen enemies with dramatic visual effect. Score 0 if no special ability exists.
The player has a health or shield system that depletes when hit, with visible damage feedback and a game-over state when depleted. Score 0 if the player is invincible.
At least 5 distinct enemy types with different behaviors: rushers, ranged shooters, shielded tanks, splitters, and support units. Score 0 if only one enemy type exists.
Enemy formations vary across waves: single-direction rushes, pincer attacks, surrounding swarms, shielded columns with support behind. Score 0 if enemies always spawn randomly with no formation.
At least 5 distinct upgrades available between waves covering fire rate, damage, spread, shield repair, deployable items, and special ability charges. Score 0 if no upgrades exist.
Boss waves appear every 5 waves featuring a large enemy with multi-phase attacks and support units, distinct from regular waves. Score 0 if no boss waves exist.
A results screen shows waves survived, total enemies destroyed, upgrades purchased, and highest wave reached. Score 0 if the game ends abruptly with no summary.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, difficulty selection, and military-themed imagery. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to wave combat to between-wave shop to boss waves to results without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.
The HUD clearly shows health/shield, wave number, enemy count, currency, and special ability charges in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine game state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: firing shows muzzle effects, kills trigger explosions, wave-start has an announcement, damage shows hit flash, and upgrades visibly change the weapon. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, arena, enemies, HUD, shop, and results with a consistent military-action palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
The player character, enemies, projectiles, arena elements, and upgrade icons use real sprite art with distinct designs. Score 0 if primary gameplay elements are unstyled rectangles.
Animation brings combat to life: enemy movement animations, explosion particles, projectile trails, wave-start effects, and boss phase transitions. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with military frames, custom fonts, or tactical-styled elements rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
